text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc said Tuesday it had purchased about $50 million of its common stock, completing a repurchase authorization previously granted by its board.
The company also announced the signing of contracts on three of its second-generation semisubmersible drilling rigs.

It said 893,000 shares were purchased in open market transactions in February. Following the completion of the repurchases, the company had 50,638,548 common shares outstanding (51,351,548 issued) as compared to 51,522,985 shares issued and outstanding as of December 31, 1996.
The Sonat D-F 97 is employed by Burlington Resources Inc, also in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, with contract expiration expected in July.

The Sonat D-F 97 will undergo a water depth upgrade to 2,350 feet following the start of the new contract with Texaco. The upgrade is generally limited to mooring system enhancements and will be performed on location with no more than seven days of downtime expected. A similar upgrade was completed on the Sonat D-F 96 in January, Transocean said.

The Transocean Discoverer has been contracted by Talisman Energy Inc to drill eight wells over a period of up to 22 months on Talisman's Ross Field Development project located in the U.K. sector of the North Sea. Revenues to be generated over the contract period are estimated at $61.4 million.

Transocean said the Discoverer is expected to commence work under the new contract in December 1997, following the completion of its present commitment with Amerada Hess Corp, also in the U.K. sector of the North Sea.
